entries.proposition: The paper states in its own Results that the Wwox knockout samples carry too few substitutions for any clock-like signature to be detected in them - i.e. the Wwox arm of the study is underpowered for the study's own endpoint.
entries.snippet: The Wwox ko cells show very few SBSs, far too few to detect the clock‐like SBSs.
entries.anchor: Results, the paragraph reporting the SigProfilerAssignment analysis of Figure 3

entries.proposition: Under SigProfilerExtractor the authors explicitly record a NEGATIVE result in the Wwox samples: no SBS40 of any sub-type was observed in either Wwox knockout or Wwox wild-type samples.
entries.snippet: We did not observe SBS40 or SBS40 a,b,c in these Wwox ko or wt samples.
entries.anchor: Results, the paragraph reporting Figure S1 (SigProfilerExtractor)

entries.proposition: The attribution of SBS40c to WWOX is made by an argument from co-deletion inside FHIT-knockout cells, not by observing SBS40c in a WWOX-knockout sample. The authors' own connective is 'suggesting'.
entries.snippet: suggesting that SBS40c might be due to Wwox loss in the Fhit ko cells
entries.anchor: Results, the numbered list of reasons following the Figure 3 description

entries.proposition: The Results section closes by asserting that WWOX/FRA16D loss underlies SBS40c accumulation 'in these mouse knockout tissues and cells' - a conclusion stated at a strength the Wwox-genotype data in this paper do not reach.
entries.snippet: We conclude from the mutational signature profiles in cells and tissues that Fhit/Fra3B loss or deletion underlies SBS5 and Wwox/Fra16D loss likely underlies SBS40c mutation accumulation in these mouse knockout tissues and cells.
entries.anchor: Results, final sentence of the section

entries.proposition: In the Discussion the same attribution is stated more weakly and conditionally, and its premise - that Fhit inactivation carries Wwox inactivation with it - is named.
entries.snippet: where SBS40c could have been contributed by Wwox loss, since Fhit inactivation regularly is associated with Wwox inactivation
entries.anchor: Discussion, first paragraph

entries.proposition: A filtering step removes every variant seen in any wild-type mouse from ALL samples before signature analysis, which by construction depletes the wild-type comparison group that the knockout groups are then contrasted against.
entries.snippet: Additionally, variants that were present in any of our WT mice were removed from all samples prior to mutational signature analysis.

skills_considered.reason: The route for the reading itself: structured surface first, section-by-section coverage, figures as pixels, locators captured while the document was open.

Cascade never needed. Europe PMC fullTextXML returned the JATS at the first request (HTTP 200, 90040 bytes) and supplementaryFiles returned the whole figure and supplement set in one archive. Invoking an acquisition cascade for an article that resolves on the first lawful call would have been ceremony.

🔴 R4 THRESHOLD CHECK RUN MECHANICALLY, NOT ASSUMED. All 18 claims carrying `Status: consolidated baseline` were enumerated from claim_registry_current.md and their titles read: CLAIM 002,003,004,005,006,007,008,012,014,015,017,018,019,020,021,022,023,024. Every one is WWOX-DEE neurobiology, human genotype-phenotype, prenatal cortical development, network physiology, myelin, or WW-domain biochemistry. None concerns somatic mutation burden, mutational signatures, clock-like signatures or the FHIT/WWOX co-loss axis. The only registry record this reading bears on is CLAIM 029, whose Status is `in observation`, not `consolidated baseline`; and the transfer verdict is ESPANSIONE/T3, which cannot justify a MAJOR working-model bump. R4 is therefore NOT triggered. Recorded rather than skipped silently, because the finding here is counter-directional and the temptation to skip the check is exactly where it would be skipped.

Considered seriously and declined. The paper yields no biomarker, molecule, pathway correction or repurposing lead: its only WWOX-directed output is a negative about a mutational-signature attribution, and a negative of that shape belongs in the dossier and the dismissal-adjacent record, not in the discovery ledger as capital. One methodological lead IS carried forward and is recorded as a discovery-ledger entry rather than a discovery sweep.
No molecule, no dose, no endpoint, no target engagement. T3/ESPANSIONE material cannot mature a therapeutic lever.
No compound is named or promoted anywhere in this reading.
Wave order was fixed by the dispatch; a single assigned PMID has no ordering decision to make.
Run at the end of the wave, before capability-scout and before the closing report.

group_assessment.weighting: 🔴 THIS IS THE HUEBNER LABORATORY'S PAPER, NOT THE AQEILAN LABORATORY'S, and the lot being an Aqeilan sweep is exactly why that is stated first. Measured today: Huebner K 408 publications, 131 with FHIT, 32 with WWOX - a FHIT laboratory of thirty years' standing, for which WWOX is the adjacent second fragile site. Aqeilan RI (137 publications, 65 on WWOX, 14 on epilepsy/encephalopathy) appears third-from-first as the contributor of one tissue set; Aldaz CM (38 on WWOX) contributed the P47T kidneys. Consequences applied throughout: (a) the Fhit material - the knockout, the ageing cohort, the tumour spectrum, the exome pipeline - is this group's own long-standing system and its observation is weighted first-hand; (b) every step that carries an observation made in Fhit-knockout cells ACROSS to a statement about WWOX is weighted as interpretation, because the WWOX arm is contributed material analysed by a FHIT laboratory and the paper's WWOX conclusion is reached by an argument about co-deletion rather than by a WWOX-genotype contrast; (c) primary for the gene is not primary for the disease, and this group is primary for neither WWOX nor WWOX-DEE - there is no human subject, no patient, no neurological phenotype and no reference-genotype variant anywhere in the study.

field_density.note: Measured today, not carried forward. The WWOX x mutational-signature intersection is 18 records against a 707-record WWOX field - a genuinely thin corner, which is why this single paper carries disproportionate weight in it and why the strength of its WWOX conclusion matters more than its citation count would suggest.

corpus_crossquery.query: Does anything already in this corpus read a mutational-signature, somatic-mutation-burden or clock-like-signature result for WWOX, and does any existing claim record a WWOX genome-stability direction that this paper's Wwox-genotype data would bear on?
corpus_crossquery.note: Two surfaces answered and the first answer is an absence that matters. (1) ZERO of the 43 fulltext dossiers and ZERO of the 70 deepdive manifests mention a mutational signature, SBS40, SBS5 or a clock-like signature: this reading is the corpus's first contact with the mutational-signature axis for WWOX, so there is no prior reading to agree or disagree with, and the negative recorded here is the corpus's only datum on it. (2) claim_registry_current.md CLAIM 029 - `in observation`, 'WWOX contributes directly to DNA-damage-response competence and genome-stability maintenance' - is the one record this reading bears on; its source is PMID 25331887 via PAPER 030. This paper does not test ATM activation or relocalization and so does not touch CLAIM 029's mechanism; what it adds is a null at the phenotypic end of the same axis, in the one panel where Wwox wild-type and Wwox knockout are plotted side by side. Recorded as qualification, not as reversal. Additionally noted while cross-querying, and reported rather than repaired: PAPER 007 (Hussain 2023 P47T), the registry source of consolidated baseline CLAIM 006 and CLAIM 007, carries `Identifier: pending normalization`, and its recorded Full title is not the title of any single article.

figure_extractions.method: PyMuPDF Document.extract_image() over the xref table of the Europe PMC render PDF
figure_extractions.note: 🔴 WHY THIS ROUTE AND NOT THE ARCHIVE JPEGs. The Europe PMC supplementaryFiles archive distributes the three main figures at 532x378, 496x662 and 532x335 - too coarse to read a 96-substitution signature panel or to segment a stacked bar. The render PDF embeds the same three figures as image streams at roughly four times that linear resolution. extract_image returns the EMBEDDED STREAM, not a rasterisation of the page, so these are the deposit's own figure bytes at the highest resolution this deployment can lawfully reach. Both versions are fingerprinted above and the archive JPEGs are retained rather than discarded. PyMuPDF became available in this deployment only for this wave; in wave 1 this article's figures would have been read at 532 px or declared unrecoverable.

page_renders.note: Supplementary Figure 1 is vector and carries no embedded raster, so the pixels have to be produced rather than extracted.
